method_card.title: Free-Time Activities and Hobbies
method_card.content:
This lesson covers how to talk about hobbies and free-time activities using faire de and jouer à/de, plus adverbs of frequency and opinion phrases.

FrenchEnglish
faire de la natationto go swimming
faire du véloto go cycling
faire du sportto do sport
faire les magasinsto go shopping
jouer au footballto play football
jouer au tennisto play tennis
jouer aux jeux vidéoto play video games
jouer de la guitareto play the guitar
toujoursalways
souventoften
quelquefoissometimes
rarementrarely
ne…jamaisnever

Grammar: faire is irregular (je fais, tu fais, il fait, nous faisons, vous faites, ils font). Use faire de for activities, jouer à for team sports/games, jouer de for instruments. Remember: de + le = du, de + la = de la, à + le = au, à + les = aux.

Model: Le week-end, je joue souvent au football avec mes amis car c'est amusant. Je fais aussi de la natation le samedi. (At the weekend, I often play football with my friends because it's fun. I also go swimming on Saturdays.)
steps: Learn the key vocabulary for hobbies and free-time activities
Master faire de vs jouer à vs jouer de with correct articles
Use adverbs of frequency to add detail to your answers
Give opinions with reasons using parce que / car + adjective
Practice combining activities, frequency and opinions in full sentences

worked_examples.question: Translate to English: 'Je fais de la natation le samedi avec ma sœur.'

steps.label: Identify the verb
steps.content: fais comes from faire (to do/make). Je fais = I do.

steps.label: Identify the activity
steps.content: faire de la natation = to go swimming. The de la is required before feminine nouns.

steps.label: Add the details
steps.content: le samedi = on Saturdays (the article le before a day means 'every'). avec ma sœur = with my sister.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: I go swimming on Saturdays with my sister.

worked_examples.question: How do you choose between faire de, jouer à, and jouer de?

steps.label: Rule 1: faire de
steps.content: Use faire de for general activities and individual sports: faire du sport, faire de la danse, faire de la lecture, faire du vélo.

steps.label: Rule 2: jouer à
steps.content: Use jouer à for team sports and games: jouer au football, jouer au tennis, jouer aux jeux vidéo. Remember à + le = au, à + les = aux.

steps.label: Rule 3: jouer de
steps.content: Use jouer de for musical instruments: jouer de la guitare, jouer du piano. Remember de + le = du, de + la = de la.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Activity/individual sport → faire de | Team sport/game → jouer à | Instrument → jouer de

method_card.title: Music, Film and Television
method_card.content:
This lesson covers entertainment vocabulary for music, film and TV, along with adjective agreement and the perfect tense with être.

FrenchEnglish
un chanteur / une chanteusea singer
un groupea band
une chansona song
écouter de la musiqueto listen to music
un concerta concert
un film d'actionan action film
une comédiea comedy
un film d'horreura horror film
regarder la téléto watch TV
une émissiona programme
une sériea series
aller au cinémato go to the cinema
un acteur / une actricean actor / actress

Adjective agreement: Add -e for feminine, -s for plural, -es for feminine plural. Irregular: bon → bonne, beau → belle, nouveau → nouvelle, ennuyeux → ennuyeuse.

Perfect tense with être: Verbs of movement (MRS VAN DER TRAMP) use être as auxiliary. Past participle agrees with subject: il est allé, elle est allée, ils sont allés, elles sont allées.

Model: Je suis allé(e) au cinéma samedi dernier. J'ai vu une comédie française. C'était amusante et les acteurs étaient très bons.
steps: Learn the key vocabulary for music, film genres and TV programmes
Master adjective agreement rules including irregular forms
Use the perfect tense with être for verbs of movement
Give opinions about entertainment with agreed adjectives
Combine past tense experiences with opinions for exam answers

method_card.title: Sport and Sporting Events
method_card.content:
This lesson covers sport vocabulary, describing past sporting events, and the imperfect tense for descriptions and habitual actions.

FrenchEnglish
le footballfootball
le rugbyrugby
le tennistennis
la natationswimming
l'athlétisme (m)athletics
le cyclismecycling
un matcha match
une compétitiona competition
gagnerto win
perdreto lose
s'entraînerto train
le maillot jaunethe yellow jersey

Imperfect tense: Take the nous form of present tense, remove -ons, add: -ais, -ais, -ait, -ions, -iez, -aient. Exception: être → stem ét-. Key phrases: c'était (it was), il y avait (there was/were), j'étais (I was), il faisait (the weather was).

Model: L'année dernière, je suis allé(e) à un match de football. Il y avait beaucoup de monde et c'était passionnant. Mon équipe a gagné trois à zéro!
steps: Learn the key vocabulary for sports and sporting events
Master the imperfect tense formation and key phrases
Combine perfect tense (events) with imperfect (descriptions)
Know key facts about the Tour de France
Practice describing a past sporting event using both tenses

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — sport appears frequently in Listening and Reading

worked_examples.question: Translate to English: 'Mon équipe de rugby a gagné le match.'

steps.label: Identify the subject
steps.content: Mon équipe de rugby = my rugby team.

steps.label: Identify the tense
steps.content: a gagné is the perfect tense of gagner (to win). Avoir + past participle.

steps.label: Complete the translation
steps.content: le match = the match.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: My rugby team won the match.

worked_examples.question: When do you use the imperfect vs the perfect tense?

steps.label: Perfect tense
steps.content: Use the perfect tense for completed, one-off actions: J'ai joué au football. (I played football.) Mon équipe a gagné. (My team won.)

steps.label: Imperfect tense
steps.content: Use the imperfect tense for descriptions, atmosphere, feelings, weather, and habitual actions: C'était passionnant. (It was exciting.) Il y avait beaucoup de monde. (There were lots of people.) Je jouais au football tous les jours. (I used to play football every day.)

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Perfect = what happened (events). Imperfect = what it was like (descriptions, atmosphere, habits).

method_card.content:
This lesson covers the main French festivals, celebration vocabulary, and the cultural context behind each event.

FrenchEnglish
NoëlChristmas

les feux d'artificefireworks
le défiléparade
on célèbrepeople celebrate
on mangepeople eat
on dansepeople dance

Grammar: The pronoun on means 'people', 'we' or 'they' in general and takes the il/elle verb form. It is very useful for describing customs: on célèbre, on mange, on danse.

Model: Pour Noël, on décore le sapin, on mange un grand repas en famille et on ouvre les cadeaux le matin du 25 décembre. C'est ma fête préférée!

method_card.title: Customs and How We Celebrate
method_card.content:
This lesson covers French customs, wedding traditions, using three tenses for celebrations, and direct object pronouns.

FrenchEnglish
faire la biseto greet with a kiss on the cheek
un mariagea wedding
se marierto get married
féliciterto congratulate
un(e) invité(e)a guest
la mairietown hall
le repasthe meal
les discoursspeeches
le muguetlily of the valley
les Journées du patrimoineHeritage Days
avant / pendant / aprèsbefore / during / after

Direct object pronouns: me, te, le/la/l', nous, vous, les. Placed before the conjugated verb: On la célèbre le 14 juillet. (People celebrate it on 14th July.) Before an infinitive: Je veux les voir.

Model: Ma cousine s'est mariée l'été dernier. D'abord, on est allés à la mairie. Ensuite, on a mangé et on a dansé. C'était génial!
steps: Learn vocabulary for customs: la bise, weddings, Heritage Days
Use three tenses when describing celebrations (present, perfect, future/conditional)
Master direct object pronouns (le, la, les) and their position
Know French wedding customs and cultural differences
Practice writing a chronological celebration paragraph

steps.label: Identify the verb
steps.content: s'est mariée is the perfect tense of the reflexive verb se marier (to get married). The extra -e shows the subject is feminine.

steps.label: Identify the rest
steps.content: Ma cousine = my cousin (female). L'été dernier = last summer.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: My cousin got married last summer.

worked_examples.question: How do direct object pronouns work in French?

steps.label: Identify the direct object
steps.content: The direct object is the noun receiving the action: On célèbre la fête.

steps.label: Replace with pronoun
steps.content: Replace la fête (feminine singular) with la: On la célèbre.

steps.label: Position rule
steps.content: The pronoun goes before the conjugated verb. With an infinitive, it goes before the infinitive: Je veux la voir.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Direct object pronouns (le/la/les) replace the noun and go before the conjugated verb (or before the infinitive).

method_card.content:
This lesson covers restaurant vocabulary, ordering food, role-play preparation, and partitive articles.

FrenchEnglish
réserver une tableto reserve a table
commanderto order
le serveur / la serveusethe waiter / waitress
la cartethe menu
l'entrée (f)the starter
le plat principalthe main course
le dessertdessert
l'addition (f)the bill
un pourboirea tip
le pouletchicken
le poissonfish
délicieux / délicieusedelicious

Partitive articles: du (masc.), de la (fem.), de l' (before vowel), des (plural) = 'some'. After a negative, all become de/d': Je mange du fromage → Je ne mange pas de fromage.

Key phrase: Je voudrais (I would like) + food/drink for polite ordering.

Model: Je voudrais réserver une table pour deux. Comme entrée, je prends la soupe. Comme plat principal, je voudrais du poulet avec des frites.
steps: Learn restaurant vocabulary for ordering, courses and the bill
Master partitive articles (du, de la, de l', des) and the negative rule
Use je voudrais as a polite ordering phrase
Prepare question structures for the role-play (Est-ce que…?, Avez-vous…?)
Practice a full restaurant role-play scenario

exam_context.frequency: Very common — restaurant role-play is a frequent Speaking task

worked_examples.question: How do you order food politely in French?

steps.label: Key phrase
steps.content: Use je voudrais (I would like) — this is the conditional of vouloir and is polite.

steps.label: For starters
steps.content: Comme entrée, je voudrais la soupe. (For starter, I would like the soup.)

steps.label: For main course
steps.content: Comme plat principal, je prends le poulet avec des frites. (For main, I'll have the chicken with chips.)

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Use je voudrais + food item, or je prends + food item. Specify the course with comme entrée / comme plat principal / comme dessert.

worked_examples.question: Why does 'du fromage' become 'de fromage' after a negative?

steps.label: The rule
steps.content: After a negative (ne…pas, ne…plus, ne…jamais), all partitive articles (du, de la, de l', des) change to de (or d' before a vowel).

steps.label: Example
steps.content: Je mange du fromage. → Je ne mange pas de fromage.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: In negative sentences, partitive articles all become de. This is because you are saying you eat 'none of' the item.

gaps.correct_explain: After ne…pas, all partitive articles become de: pas de viande.

wrong.de la: de la is the partitive for feminine nouns, but after a negative it changes to de.

gaps.correct_explain: du is the partitive for masculine nouns. Poisson is masculine: du poisson = some fish.

wrong.de: de is only used after a negative. This clause is positive (je mange), so use the full partitive du.

gaps.correct_explain: des is the partitive for plural nouns. Légumes is plural: des légumes = some vegetables.

wrong.de: de is only used after a negative. This clause is positive, so use the full partitive des.
